accuracy.evidence: Forms checked against CCSS ELA L.4.1b (I was walking; I am walking; I will be walking) and the national curriculum in England English Appendix 2, Year 2 (progressive form of verbs in the present and past tense: she is drumming, he was shouting). Every HELP item pairs the time clue with the right be form and subject number (I am, the dog is, they were, Sam was, she/we will be). -ing spellings follow Appendix 1 rules: doubling after a single short vowel + single consonant (running, swimming, sitting, hopping), dropping final e (making, writing), y kept (playing). State verbs (know, want, like) are described as not usually taking -ing, which is the standard hedge, not an absolute rule.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented learner errors with progressive forms: will without be (prediction 1, SLIP 3, challenge q3), was with a plural subject (HELP feedback for they/we, SLIP 1, m4), be without -ing (SLIP 2, she is play), missing be, progressive with state verbs (SLIP 4 I am knowing, challenge q6, m6), present progressive used for habits or habits read as 'now' (step 3 and its prediction), the quick event put in the progressive (step 4), and -ing spelling slips (makeing, runing, writting, dropped g in runnin/sittin, hoping for hopping).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagongo is built on the progressive aspect itself: dragging be-form helpers (including the decoy will) onto a past/now/future timeline that then shows an ongoing bar, sorting cards into a 'going on now' bar versus a row of habit dots, and dragging the long action onto a bar while the quick event takes a dot (the interrupted past progressive). flagtense (411: -ed spelling, is/are/was/were, irregular past) and flagpperf (756: has/have + participle, gone/been) cover other tenses; the lab_distinct gate passed under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Feedback explains the rule rather than revealing the answer: choosing are for 'At 3 pm yesterday' returns 'are is for now. The clue "At 3 pm yesterday" points to the past'; was for they returns 'they means more than one, so use were'; will returns 'will on its own is not enough... will be + -ing'; dropping the habit card in 'now' returns 'There is no be + -ing here...' plus the clue word; choosing the quick event as the long action explains that it happens at one moment and takes the simple past (rang, fell).

predictions.evidence: Four predictions, each with a tempting wrong option disproved by the task: 'will' for the future progressive (the will tile is wrong in HELP 3 and 6), 'makeing' (ING 2 rejects it), 'yes' the person in 'I walk to school' is walking now (step 3 sorts walk every day as a habit), and 'the ringing' started first (step 4 puts the reading on the long bar). A.reveal names the learner's locked-in pick when each task completes.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with twelve wrong-answer messages that name the slip: are for a past clue, was with we, sings read as now, sang as finished, will without be, am for a future clue, hoping vs hopping, hopeing, ran for the long action, is running with a past event, I am knowing (state verb) and a missing helper.

readability.evidence: learn/readability.py: kid FK grade 1.3 (family limit 5.0), adult 8.1 (limit 10.0). Kid paragraphs use one example each (I am reading; we were swimming; I eat lunch at noon; she was reading when the phone rang). Terms present participle and Common Core codes stay in the adult text; canvas prompts are one short line.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph has one job (form, time, now vs habit, interrupted action plus spelling); the adult text gives the curriculum source, the three uses with examples, named mistakes and what the lab does. The content gate found no filler phrases and the explanation is under 12% similar to every other lesson, including 411 and 794.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android screenshots in light and dark for all six steps, and wrong-answer states (was in 'Right now I', runing, a habit drop, the phone ringing as the long action, a correct word tapped). After moving the -ing options up and replacing the step 4 instruction with the feedback, nothing overlaps or clips; helper tiles wrap into two rows of at least 50 px. Walkthrough passed on iPhone 13.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag has a button under the canvas: 'Put were in the gap', 'Spell it running', 'Put the card in going on now', 'reading a book was the long action', 'was is the slip'. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after every action with the feedback, the challenge feedback is a role=status live region, warnings switch to #fda4af on the dark canvas, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
